label: input token j in the middle of the original phase (t=3..6)
explanation: Token detector for the letter j. 38500 of 38502 dev activations fall on steps where the input is j during the original phase. It never fires in the delimiter or copy phase, not even when j is output or fed back, and it never fires at t=0 or 1. Activity is strongest at t=3..5 (lift about 4x, 89% of mass), weak at t=2 and 6, and close to zero at t=7+. Within those steps only about half to 70% of j inputs activate, so precision is the incomplete part. Magnitude depends on the prefix. The top activations come after earlier f, o, d or 0 tokens (e.g. o f f f j). Restricting to prefixes that contain f/o/d/0 raises precision to 0.68 but loses recall, so this context effect is graded rather than a clean condition. A repeated j (in_first=0) fires less often (rate 0.2x). Any other input token gives essentially no activation.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: j, -, a, v, <DEL>, 3; least: p, b, z, x) and the first original token (most: f, 0, o, d, a, c; least: j, k, s, y); timing cues that raise it most: t=4, t=5, t=3.
